messages:
IncidentBot: P1 alert -> INC-20260315-043 | serve-us-west2 high-err-rate + node-flap detected. Autoscaler swung 8->44->9 in ~8m.
Aisha: grabbing pager. Who's on-call for runtime? @tom? :eyes:
Tom: oncall here. Looking at cluster metrics now. Heap of CrashLoopBackOffs on serve-runtime.
Diego: logs show GPU init failures: ```2026-03-15T11:15:12Z runtime: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED; stack trace...``` Also a bunch of OOMKilled during init.
Aisha: customer impact: multiple gen endpoints up to 10x latency, streaming sessions stuck. CS reports 4 enterprise customers with real-time degradation.
Tom: autoscaler events: ```Scale from 8 to 44 (reason: unschedulable pods) at 11:11, scale down to 9 at 11:18 due to utilization low -> repeat```. Looks like pods crash during startup causing requeues which retrigger scaling.
Diego: also seeing node GPU resets on nodes gpu-usw2-7 and gpu-usw2-10 around the same timestamps. Could be a flaky driver or thermal issue.
Aisha: immediate mitigation steps: 1) pause autoscaler 2) reduce max nodes to 12 3) cordon noisy nodes 4) roll a quick init container memory bump 5) post status. I'll execute pause.
Aisha: running: `./infra/k8s/scripts/pause-autoscaler --pause`
OpsBot: autoscaler paused by Aisha at 2026-03-15T11:20:05Z (reason: incident INC-20260315-043)
Tom: cordoned gpu-usw2-7, gpu-usw2-10. Evicting pods gracefully. Starting controlled rollout of serve-runtime with init memory 2.4Gi (was 1.4Gi) in canary.
Diego: attaching a sample pod error: ```Pod serve-runtime-xyz stderr: malloc failed: required=1.9Gi > limit=1.5Gi -> OOMKilled``` Also nvidia-smi shows GPU reset count incremented.
Aisha: CS-Bot: update status page: "We are mitigating an ongoing issue impacting serving in us-west-2; some customers may see errors/latency. Engineers are actively investigating."
CS-Bot: Status updated to INCIDENT (11:25 UTC) by Aisha. Targeted emails queued for affected customers.
Tom: canary looks good (0/3 CUBLAS errors). Rolling to 25% then 60% with 30s interval.
Diego: suggestion: add exponential startup backoff to runtime's init probe to avoid immediate crashloop -> reduces requeues. Also recommend increase scaleDownStabilization to 300s and scaleUpDelay to 120s.
Aisha: agreed. I've opened infra ticket #INFRA-785 to adjust autoscaler policy and instrument GPU-reset metric. Assign Tom. ETA 48h.
Tom: after pause and cordon, node count held at 11 and error rate dropped from 9% -> 1.2%. Streaming sessions recovered for most customers.
Diego: note: we still have two pods that fail with driver-reset during runtime attach. Those pods are pinned to cordoned nodes; I'll file hardware ticket and tie to telemetry.
Aisha: leaving commands for post-incident notes:
```
kubectl get events -n redwood-runtime --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 50
kubectl describe pod serve-runtime-xyz -n redwood-runtime
kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu-usw2
helm upgrade redwood-runtime infra/serve --set init.memory=2.4Gi --namespace redwood-runtime
```
Tom: IncidentBot: marking incident mitigated -> severity lowered to P2. Handoff to daytime oncall. Please monitor GPU reset metric and autoscaler behavior for 2h.
IncidentBot: INC-20260315-043 status=mitigated | severity=P2 | handoff=oncall-day(shift) at 2026-03-15T11:33:20Z
Aisha: adding owners for follow-ups: Diego -> driver investigation/hardware ticket; Tom -> autoscaler tuning + runbook update; Aisha -> customer postmortem + timeline. Draft due EOD.
CS-Bot: Notified affected customers with incident link https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20260315-043
Diego: creating alert: metric gpu_driver_resets > 0 spike for >2m -> paged to oncall.
Tom: final note: re-enable autoscaler after config stabilized. For now keep paused until infra change merged. Good triage team. :thumbsup:
Aisha: closing thread and moving to postmortem doc (link: https://redwood/pm/INC-20260315-043). Thanks everyone.
